Health Station: free blood pressure and health checks at Pacific Fair

Yes, you can check your blood pressure for free at the Health Station inside Priceline Pharmacy Pacific Fair in Broadbeach, along with your weight, BMI and type 2 diabetes risk. There’s no appointment and no charge, and a pharmacist is nearby to explain what your numbers mean. Just come in any day we’re open.

Call (07) 5592 2099 Hours & directions

At a glance

What it is
Self-service health checks at the Health Station inside the store, with a pharmacist nearby to explain results.
Who it's for
Anyone. Worth checking each time you fill a script.

Free.
How long
A few minutes.
Booking
No appointment needed.
How to book
Just come in during opening hours.

What can I check at the Health Station?

Blood pressure

High blood pressure usually has no symptoms, which is why regular checks matter. It’s a major risk factor for heart attack, stroke and kidney disease.

Height, weight and BMI

A quick way to track changes over time. BMI is a rough guide only and doesn’t account for things like muscle mass.

AUSDRISK: type 2 diabetes risk

A short questionnaire that estimates your risk of developing type 2 diabetes in the next five years.

How does the Health Station work?

  • It’s free, and there’s no appointment needed. Just come in during opening hours.
  • We can email your results to you, so you can track them or share them with your doctor.
  • Check in each time you fill your scripts, and you’ll see how your health is changing over time.
  • If a result is outside the healthy range, our pharmacists can talk it through and refer you to a GP. Help Medical is an independent general practice located inside our store.

What do blood pressure numbers mean?

A reading has two numbers, for example 120/80. The top number is the pressure when your heart beats; the bottom number is the pressure between beats. A single high reading doesn’t mean you have high blood pressure, but it’s a sign to check again and talk to your doctor.

When should I see a doctor straight away?

If you have a very high reading along with chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, weakness, or changes in vision or speech, call 000.

What else can help?

If your numbers suggest a change is worth making, our pharmacists offer free weight management support. If you have diabetes, we’re an access point for NDSS supplies. And if you take several medicines, a free medication review checks they’re all working well together.

Common questions

Is the Health Station free?

Yes. Blood pressure, height, weight, BMI and type 2 diabetes risk checks at the Health Station are all free. Just come in any day we’re open.

Do I need to book a blood pressure check?

No. Just come in during opening hours and use the Health Station. A pharmacist is nearby to explain your results.

What can I check at the Health Station?

Blood pressure, height, weight and BMI, plus the AUSDRISK questionnaire, which estimates your risk of developing type 2 diabetes in the next five years. Ask a pharmacist to talk you through any result.

Can I keep a record of my results?

Yes. Ask us to email your results to you, so you can track them over time or share them with your doctor.

What do blood pressure numbers mean?

A reading has two numbers, for example 120/80. The top number is the pressure when your heart beats; the bottom number is the pressure between beats. A single high reading doesn’t mean you have high blood pressure, but it’s a sign to check again and talk to a pharmacist or your doctor.

What if my reading is outside the healthy range?

Our pharmacists can talk it through with you and refer you to a GP. Help Medical is an independent general practice located inside our store, so you can be seen without leaving the centre.

How often should I check my blood pressure?

High blood pressure usually has no symptoms, so regular checks matter. Many people find it easy to check each time they fill a script, so make it part of your next visit.
